title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the 13th Batch of Guiding Cases
ruling_gist_en: The statutory penalty referenced in the crime of using undisclosed information for trading as stipulated in Article 180(4) of the Criminal Law of the PRC shall be the full statutory penalty from paragraph 1 concerning insider trading and leaking inside information. That is, the crime of using undisclosed information for trading shall have two circumstances, namely 'serious circumstances' and 'particularly serious circumstances,' and two sentencing levels.
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the 13th Batch of Guiding Cases

Fa [2016] No. 214

To: All High People's Courts of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Sub-court of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

Upon deliberation and approval by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, the following four cases, including the case of Ma Le for using undisclosed information to trade, are hereby issued as the 13th batch of Guiding Cases (Guiding Cases No. 61-64), for reference in the trial of similar cases.

June 30, 2016

Guiding Case No. 61

Ma Le v. — crime of using undisclosed information to trade

(Deliberated and approved by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, issued on June 30, 2016)

Keywords: Criminal / Crime of using undisclosed information to trade / Reference to statutory punishment / Especially serious circumstances

Ruling Gist

The reference to statutory punishment prescribed in paragraph 4 of Article 180 of the Criminal Law of the PRC for the crime of using undisclosed information to trade shall be a reference to all statutory punishments under paragraph 1 for the crimes of insider trading and disclosure of inside information. That is, the crime of using undisclosed information to trade shall have two circumstances: "serious circumstances" and "especially serious circumstances," corresponding to two sentencing ranges.

Related Law

Article 180 of the Criminal Law of the PRC

Basic Facts

During the period from March 9, 2011 to May 30, 2013, the defendant Ma Le served as the fund manager of the Boshi Select Stock Securities Investment Fund under Boshi Fund Management Co., Ltd., with full authority over the investment fund's stock market trading. He obtained undisclosed information regarding the target stocks, trading times, and trading volumes of the Boshi Select Stock Securities Investment Fund. During his tenure, Ma Le used the aforementioned undisclosed information under his control to engage in securities trading activities related to that information. He manipulated three stock accounts under his control, under the names "Jin", "Yan A", and "Yan B", using prepaid unregistered Shenzhouxing phone cards to place orders. He bought and sold the same 76 stocks before (1-5 trading days), simultaneously with, or slightly after (1-2 trading days) the "Boshi Select" fund account he managed, with a cumulative transaction amount of over RMB 1.05 billion, and an illegal profit of RMB 18,833,374.74. On July 17, 2013, Ma Le voluntarily surrendered himself to the Shenzhen Public Security Bureau and truthfully confessed his crimes upon arrival, constituting voluntary surrender. Ma Le demonstrated a good attitude of admitting guilt, and the illegal gains could be fully returned from the seized and frozen assets, and the imposed fine could also be fully paid.

Judgment

The Criminal Judgment (2014) Shen Zhong Fa Xing Er Chu Zi No. 27 of the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province held that the conduct of the defendant Ma Le constituted the crime of using undisclosed information to trade. However, the Criminal Law does not provide for "especially serious circumstances" for the crime of using undisclosed information to trade. Therefore, Ma Le's conduct could only be found to constitute "serious circumstances." Ma Le voluntarily surrendered and could be given a lighter punishment according to law. Ma Le demonstrated a good attitude of admitting guilt, the illegal gains could be fully returned, and the fine could be fully paid, showing genuine repentance. Furthermore, based on an investigation and assessment by the Community Correction and Placement Assistance Section of the Futian District Judicial Bureau of Shenzhen, declaring a suspended sentence for Ma Le would not have a significant adverse impact on the community in which he resides, meeting the conditions for a suspended sentence. Consequently, Ma Le was sentenced to three years of fixed-term imprisonment, suspended for five years, and fined RMB 18.84 million; the illegal gains of RMB 18,833,374.74 were ordered to be recovered and turned over to the state treasury.

After the judgment was pronounced, the Shenzhen People's Procuratorate filed a protest, arguing that the conduct of the defendant Ma Le should be determined as having especially serious circumstances and punished according to the "especially serious circumstances" sentencing range. The first-instance judgment incorrectly applied the law and the sentence was manifestly improper, and should be corrected according to law.

The Criminal Ruling (2014) Yue Gao Fa Xing Er Zhong Zi No. 137 of the Guangdong High People's Court held that paragraph 4 of Article 180 of the Criminal Law provides that if the use of undisclosed information to trade constitutes serious circumstances, punishment shall be imposed in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 1. This provision does not specify "especially serious circumstances" for the crime of using undisclosed information to trade. According to paragraph 1 of Article 180, for serious circumstances, the punishment is fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years or criminal detention, and a fine of not less than one time but not more than five times the illegal gains, or a fine alone. Therefore, Ma Le's use of undisclosed information to trade constituted serious circumstances, and the sentence should be imposed within that sentencing range. The original judgment had an appropriate sentence, and the protesting authority's protest grounds were not established and were not adopted. The ruling dismissed the protest and affirmed the original judgment.

After the second-instance ruling became effective, the Guangdong People's Procuratorate requested the Supreme People's Procuratorate to file a protest with the Supreme People's Court under the trial supervision procedure. The Supreme People's Procuratorate protested, arguing that paragraph 4 of Article 180 of the Criminal Law constitutes a reference to statutory punishment and should refer to all punishment provisions of paragraph 1; the illegality and liability for the crime of using undisclosed information to trade are equivalent to those for the crimes of insider trading and disclosure of inside information, and the statutory punishments should be equivalent; Ma Le's conduct should be determined as having especially serious circumstances, and imposing a suspended sentence on him was manifestly improper. The final ruling in this case, on the ground that paragraph 4 of Article 180 of the Criminal Law does not provide for "especially serious circumstances" for the crime of using undisclosed information to trade, downgraded the evaluation of Ma Le's criminal conduct, which constituted an error in the application of law leading to an improper sentence, and should be corrected according to law.

The Supreme People's Court formed a collegial panel according to law to directly retry the case and held a public hearing. The facts found upon retrial were essentially the same as the original trial, but the original trial found that the defendant Ma Le's illegal gains amounted to RMB 18,833,374.74, which was a calculation error. The actual amount was RMB 19,120,246.98, and should be corrected according to law. The Criminal Judgment (2015) Xing Kang Zi No. 1 of the Supreme People's Court held that the conduct of the defendant Ma Le constituted the crime of using undisclosed information to trade. Ma Le used undisclosed information to trade 76 stocks, with a cumulative transaction amount of over RMB 1.05 billion and illegal gains of over RMB 19.12 million, which fell under especially serious circumstances. Considering that Ma Le voluntarily returned to China from abroad and surrendered himself, meeting the statutory mitigating or lenient circumstances for voluntary surrender; that before being controlled, he converted the stocks into cash and deposited it in the three involved accounts, voluntarily explained the situation to the China Securities Regulatory Commission, returned all illegal gains, showed a good attitude of admitting guilt and repentance, did not squander the illicit funds, and the original fine had been fully paid, and other discretionary lenient circumstances, a mitigated punishment could be imposed on Ma Le. The facts were clearly found, the evidence was reliable and sufficient, and the conviction was correct in the first-instance judgment and the second-instance ruling. However, due to a misunderstanding of the legal provision, the sentence was improper and should be corrected. In accordance with paragraph 4 and paragraph 1 of Article 180, paragraph 1 of Article 67, Articles 52, 53, and 64 of the Criminal Law of the PRC, and subparagraph (3) of Article 389 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment was as follows: 1. The conviction part for the defendant Ma Le in the Criminal Ruling (2014) Yue Gao Fa Xing Er Zhong Zi No. 137 of the Guangdong High People's Court and the Criminal Judgment (2014) Shen Zhong Fa Xing Er Chu Zi No. 27 of the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court was affirmed; 2. The sentencing part and the part regarding recovery of illegal gains for the defendant Ma Le in the Criminal Ruling (2014) Yue Gao Fa Xing Er Zhong Zi No. 137 of the Guangdong High People's Court and the Criminal Judgment (2014) Shen Zhong Fa Xing Er Chu Zi No. 27 of the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court were reversed; 3. The defendant Ma Le was guilty of the crime of using undisclosed information to trade, sentenced to three years of fixed-term imprisonment, and fined RMB 19.13 million; 4. The illegal gains of RMB 19,120,246.98 were ordered to be recovered and turned over to the state treasury.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that: The facts of this case were clear, the conviction was correct, and the focus of the dispute was on how to correctly understand the reference by paragraph 4 of Article 180 of the Criminal Law to paragraph 1, and how to grasp the criteria for determining "especially serious circumstances" for the crime of using undisclosed information to trade.

I. Understanding and Grasping the Reference by Paragraph 4 of Article 180 of the Criminal Law to the Sentencing Circumstances of Paragraph 1

Paragraph 1 of Article 180 of the Criminal Law provides for the crimes of insider trading and disclosure of inside information: "Any insider of securities or futures trading who obtains inside information on securities or futures trading, prior to the disclosure of information that involves the issuance of securities, securities or futures trading, or other information that has a significant impact on the prices of securities or futures, buys or sells the securities, or engages in futures trading related to the inside information, or discloses the information, or explicitly or implicitly suggests that others engage in the above trading activities, if the circumstances are serious, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years or criminal detention, and concurrently or independently shall be fined not less than one time but not more than five times the illegal gains; if the circumstances are especially serious, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years but not more than ten years, and concurrently shall be fined not less than one time but not more than five times the illegal gains." Paragraph 4 provides for the crime of using undisclosed information to trade: "Any employee of a stock exchange, futures exchange, securities company, futures brokerage company, fund management company, commercial bank, insurance company, or other financial institution, or any staff member of a relevant regulatory department or self-regulatory organization, who uses other undisclosed information other than inside information obtained by virtue of his position to, in violation of regulations, engage in securities or futures trading activities related to such information, or explicitly or implicitly suggests that others engage in related trading activities, if the circumstances are serious, shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 1."

There are different understandings in judicial practice regarding how to interpret the phrase "if the circumstances are serious, shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 1" in paragraph 4. One view holds that paragraph 4 only provides for "serious circumstances" but does not provide for "especially serious circumstances"; therefore, "if the circumstances are serious, shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 1" can only refer to punishment according to the "serious circumstances" sentencing range in paragraph 1. Another view holds that "serious circumstances" in paragraph 4 is merely an element for establishing the crime, meaning that if the circumstances reach the level of serious or above, punishment shall be imposed in accordance with paragraph 1. As for the specific punishment, it depends on whether the circumstances fall under "serious" or "especially serious" under paragraph 1, and the sentence shall be imposed accordingly. For serious circumstances, "the punishment is fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years," and for especially serious circumstances, "the punishment is fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years but not more than ten years."

The Supreme People's Court held that the reference to statutory punishment in paragraph 4 of Article 180 of the Criminal Law shall be a reference to all statutory punishments under paragraph 1. That is, the crime of using undisclosed information to trade shall have two circumstances: "serious circumstances" and "especially serious circumstances," corresponding to two sentencing ranges. The specific reasons for this understanding are as follows:

(A) It conforms to the legislative purpose of the Criminal Law. In China's fund, securities, futures, and other fields, acts of using undisclosed information to trade are relatively common. Perpetrators use the substantial funds invested by the public as backing, obtaining huge illegal benefits by buying or selling in advance, shifting risks and losses to other investors. This not only damages the property interests of their employing entities but also seriously undermines the principles of openness, fairness, and justice in the securities market, severely harms the interests of client investors or retail investors in an information disadvantage, seriously damages the reputation of the financial industry, and affects investor confidence in financial institutions, thereby seriously impacting the healthy development of asset management, funds, securities, and futures markets. For this reason, the Criminal Law Amendment (VII) added the crime of using undisclosed information to trade and placed it in the same article as the crimes of insider trading and disclosure of inside information, indicating that the illegality and liability of the two crimes are equivalent. The crime of using undisclosed information to trade should also apply the "especially serious circumstances" provision.

(B) It conforms to the literal meaning of the provision. First, "serious circumstances" in paragraph 4 of Article 180 serves as an element for establishing the crime. The Provisions (II) of the Supreme People's Procuratorate and the Ministry of Public Security on the Standards for Filing Criminal Cases under the Jurisdiction of Public Security Organs for Investigation provides the circumstantial standards for initiating prosecution for the crime of using undisclosed information to trade, indicating that the crime requires reaching "serious circumstances" to be prosecuted. The crime of using undisclosed information to trade is a circumstantial crime; to clarify its nature as a circumstantial crime, the legislation must use the expression "serious circumstances" to avoid criminalizing conduct where circumstances are "not serious." Second, "serious circumstances" in this paragraph does not have the dual nature of both an element and a sentencing provision. In the Criminal Law, there are many instances where "serious circumstances" serves both as a provision for establishing the crime and as a sentencing provision, but in each such case, the specific statutory punishment is listed thereafter. In paragraph 4 of Article 180, "serious circumstances" is not followed by a specific statutory punishment; instead, reference is made to the statutory punishment for the crimes of insider trading and disclosure of inside information. Therefore, "serious circumstances" in this paragraph only has the nature of an element for establishing the crime and does not have the nature of a sentencing provision.

(C) It conforms to the understanding of the legislative technique of referencing statutory punishment. Referencing statutory punishment means that for a particular crime, independent statutory punishment is not provided, but instead, the statutory punishment of another crime is referred to as the statutory punishment for that crime. The purpose of referencing statutory punishment in paragraph 4 of Article 180 is to avoid repetition of wording in the legal provisions and does not constitute a situation of unclear legal provisions.

In conclusion, although paragraph 4 of Article 180 of the Criminal Law does not explicitly state "especially serious circumstances," based on the legislative purpose, literal meaning, and legislative technique of this paragraph, it should include the circumstance of "especially serious circumstances" and its corresponding sentencing range.

II. Criteria for Determining "Especially Serious Circumstances" for the Crime of Using Undisclosed Information to Trade

Currently, there is no specific provision on the criteria for determining "especially serious circumstances" for the crime of using undisclosed information to trade. However, given that the Criminal Law provides that the crime of using undisclosed information to trade is punishable with reference to the provisions on the crimes of insider trading and disclosure of inside information, the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Criminal Cases Involving Insider Trading and Disclosure of Inside Information considers circumstances such as a transaction amount of over RMB 2.5 million or illegal gains of over RMB 750,000 as constituting "especially serious circumstances" for the crimes of insider trading and disclosure of inside information. The crime of using undisclosed information to trade should follow the same standard. Ma Le's use of undisclosed information for trading activities had a cumulative transaction amount of over RMB 1.05 billion and illegal gains of over RMB 19.12 million, far exceeding the above standards, and was the largest amount of such crimes nationwide at the time of the incident. With reference to the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Criminal Cases Involving Insider Trading and Disclosure of Inside Information, Ma Le's criminal circumstances should be considered as "especially serious circumstances."

(Judges of the effective judgment: Luo Zhiyong, Dong Chaoyang, Li Jiantao)

Guiding Case No. 62

Wang Xinming v. — crime of contract fraud

(Deliberated and approved by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, issued on June 30, 2016)

Keywords: Criminal / Contract fraud / Amount-based crime / Completed / Attempted

Ruling Gist

In amount-based crimes, if the completed part and the attempted part of the crime correspond to different statutory punishment ranges, it shall first be determined whether to mitigate the punishment for the attempted part; the statutory punishment range corresponding to the attempted part shall be determined, and then compared with the statutory punishment range corresponding to the completed part. The heavier statutory punishment range shall be applied, and a heavier punishment may be imposed as appropriate. If both fall within the same sentencing range, a heavier punishment shall be imposed as appropriate based on the completed part.

Related Law

Article 23 of the Criminal Law of the PRC

Basic Facts

On July 29, 2012, the defendant Wang Xinming used a forged household registration booklet and identity card, impersonating the homeowner's identity (i.e., Wang Xinming's father), and at the Lianjia Real Estate Brokerage Co., Ltd. Gucheng Park Store in Shijingshan District, Beijing, he purported to sell a house located at No. 28 Gucheng Road in the district, signing a house sale contract with the victim Xu. The agreed purchase price was RMB 1 million, and he immediately collected a deposit of RMB 10,000 from Xu. On August 12, 2012, Wang Xinming further collected the first payment of RMB 290,000 from Xu, with the balance to be paid after the transfer of ownership. When the parties later went through the house transfer procedures, Wang Xinming's false identity was discovered by staff of the Shijingshan District Commission of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, and the remaining payment was not obtained. On April 23, 2013, Wang Xinming was apprehended by the public security authorities. The next day, Wang Xinming's relatives returned the illicit gains to the victim Xu, who expressed forgiveness to Wang Xinming.

Judgment

The Shijingshan District People's Court of Beijing, after trial, issued the Criminal Judgment (2013) Shi Xing Chu Zi No. 239 on August 23, 2013, holding that the conduct of the defendant Wang Xinming constituted the crime of contract fraud with a huge amount. Considering that he truthfully confessed the criminal facts, returned all illicit gains with the help of his relatives, and obtained the victim's forgiveness, a lighter punishment was imposed according to law. The procuratorial authority of the Shijingshan District People's Procuratorate of Beijing correctly stated the charges, but the allegations that the amount was especially huge and that the crime was attempted were incorrect and were corrected. The defendant Wang Xinming was convicted of contract fraud, sentenced to six years of fixed-term imprisonment, and fined RMB 6,000. After the judgment was pronounced, the procuratorial authority filed a protest, arguing that the criminal amount should be RMB 1 million, which is especially huge, and that the original judgment failed to evaluate the attempted RMB 700,000 and only determined the completed RMB 300,000 as a huge amount, constituting an error in the application of law. The First Branch of the Beijing People's Procuratorate supported the protest with the same opinion. Wang Xinming appealed on the ground that the original sentence was too heavy, but later applied to withdraw the appeal during the trial. The Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, after trial, issued the Criminal Ruling (2013) Yi Zhong Xing Zhong Zi No. 4134 on December 2, 2013: allowing the appellant Wang Xinming to withdraw the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that: Wang Xinming, with the purpose of illegal possession, signed a contract under a false name, and his conduct constituted the crime of contract fraud. The facts found by the first-instance judgment were clear, the evidence was reliable and sufficient, the characterization was correct, and the trial procedure was lawful. However, it was improper that the attempted RMB 700,000 was not evaluated, and this was corrected. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Criminal Law and judicial interpretations, considering that Wang Xinming's contract fraud completed RMB 300,000 and attempted RMB 700,000, but the punishment for the attempted part could be mitigated, that Wang Xinming truthfully confessed the criminal facts, returned all illicit gains and obtained the victim's forgiveness, and other factors, the original sentence was within the statutory punishment range, and the protesting authority did not object to the specific sentence, so it should be affirmed. The protest opinion of the Shijingshan District People's Procuratorate of Beijing and the supporting protest opinion of the First Branch of the Beijing People's Procuratorate were adopted as appropriate. Given that Wang Xinming applied to withdraw the appeal during the second instance, and the application to withdraw the appeal complied with legal provisions, the second-instance court ruled to allow the withdrawal of the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

The dispute in this case focuses on how to determine the sentence when both completed and attempted crimes coexist in a quantitative offense. Article 6 of the Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Adjudication of Criminal Cases of Fraud stipulates: "Where a fraud involves both completed and attempted acts, and each reaches a different sentencing range, the heavier punishment shall be imposed; if they reach the same sentencing range, punishment shall be imposed for the completed fraud offense." Therefore, where both completed and attempted criminal acts coexist in a quantitative offense and both constitute crimes, in determining the statutory sentencing range applicable to the entire case, the attempted portion shall first be evaluated for any reduction in punishment, thereby determining the statutory sentencing range corresponding to the attempted portion. This range shall then be compared with the statutory sentencing range corresponding to the completed portion to determine the statutory sentencing range applicable to the entire case. If the statutory sentencing range corresponding to the completed portion is heavier or the same, the statutory sentencing range corresponding to the completed portion shall be used to determine the applicable statutory sentencing range for the entire case, with other circumstances, including the attempted portion, serving as adjustment factors for determining the starting point of sentencing, thereby establishing the benchmark sentence. If the statutory sentencing range corresponding to the attempted portion is heavier, the statutory sentencing range corresponding to the attempted portion shall be used to determine the applicable statutory sentencing range for the entire case, with other circumstances, including the completed portion, together with the attempted status of the attempted portion, serving as adjustment factors for determining the starting point of sentencing, thereby establishing the benchmark sentence.

In this case, the completed portion of Wang Xinming's contract fraud offense amounted to RMB 300,000. According to the judicial interpretation and the specific enforcement standards of Beijing, the corresponding statutory sentencing range was fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than ten years. The attempted portion amounted to RMB 700,000. Considering the specific circumstances of this case, a sentence one level lower should be imposed for the attempted portion, so the statutory sentencing range for the attempted portion was also fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than ten years, which was the same as the statutory sentencing range corresponding to the completed portion of RMB 300,000. Therefore, based on the basic criminal facts of the completed contract fraud of RMB 300,000, the statutory sentencing range applicable to Wang Xinming was determined to be fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than ten years. The criminal facts of the attempted portion of RMB 700,000, together with his truthful confession of criminal facts, full restitution of the ill-gotten gains, and obtaining the victim's understanding, were all considered as sentencing circumstances. Accordingly, Wang Xinming received a lighter punishment: fixed-term imprisonment of six years and a fine of RMB 60,000.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Gao Song, Lv Jing, Wang Yan)

Guiding Case No. 63

Xu Jiafu — Application for Compulsory Medical Treatment

(Discussed and approved by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, released on June 30, 2016)

Keywords: criminal procedure / compulsory medical treatment / possibility of continuing to endanger society

Ruling Gist

In adjudicating a case for compulsory medical treatment, whether the respondent or defendant has "the possibility of continuing to endanger society" shall be determined by comprehensively considering the type and symptoms of the mental illness suffered by the respondent or defendant, whether their condition has improved at the time of trial, and whether their family members or guardians have the willingness and ability to strictly supervise and voluntarily send them for medical treatment. When necessary, an assessment may be entrusted to relevant institutions or experts.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 18, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China

Article 284 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

The respondent Xu Jiafu began exhibiting mental abnormalities in the second half of 2007, manifested by hearing voices when none were present, believing others were talking about him, that someone wanted to kill him, feeling nervous and afraid, staying awake at night, carrying a knife for self-defense, and going out to hide. As he did not receive treatment, his condition worsened. At approximately 4:00 a.m. on November 18, 2012, the respondent heard someone coming to kill him by car at his usual residence, so he carried a knife and a hammer intending to go out and commit suicide by crashing into a car. Zhang Youfa, the security guard at his residence, knowing he was going out to crash into a car to commit suicide, did not open the door for him. The respondent saw the victim holding a mobile phone and believed the victim was calling someone to harm him. The respondent immediately stabbed the victim's body with the knife he was carrying and struck the victim's head with the hammer, causing the victim's death on the spot. Forensic medical examination determined that the victim died from severe craniocerebral injury caused by a blunt force blow to the head.

On December 10, 2012, the respondent was sent by the public security authorities to the Fourth People's Hospital of Chengdu for hospitalization. On December 17, 2012, the Chengdu Jingwei Forensic Medical Institute, at the entrustment of the Wuhou Branch of the Chengdu Public Security Bureau, conducted an appraisal of the respondent's mental illness and criminal responsibility. On the 26th of the same month, the institute issued an appraisal opinion (Cheng Jing Si Jian Suo [2012] No. 105), stating: 1. The person appraised, Xu Jiafu, currently suffers from schizophrenia, hallucinatory-paranoid type; 2. The person appraised, Xu Jiafu, had no criminal responsibility when committing the act at approximately 4:00 a.m. on November 18, 2012. In January 2013, the Fourth People's Hospital of Chengdu issued a certificate regarding the respondent's condition, confirming that Xu Jiafu required continued treatment.

Judgment

The Wuhou District People's Court of Sichuan Province issued a compulsory medical treatment decision (No. 1 of 2013, Wu Hou Xing Qiang Chu Zi) on January 24, 2013: To implement compulsory medical treatment for the respondent Xu Jiafu.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held: After the respondent Xu Jiafu committed a violent act of intentional homicide, he was determined, through appraisal, to be a mentally ill person who bears no criminal responsibility according to law. His behavior of carrying defensive tools such as knives when going out, due to his delusion that others intended to harm him, and given that his condition had not improved and required continued treatment, it was determined that if released into society, he would have the possibility of continuing to endanger society. The application filed by the Wuhou District People's Procuratorate of Chengdu City for compulsory medical treatment of the respondent was valid and was supported. The agent ad litem argued that whether the respondent had the possibility of continuing to endanger society should be assessed by a medical institution, and that in this case there was no assessment report from a medical institution, and the evidence for compulsory medical treatment of the respondent was insufficient. The court held that in compulsory medical treatment, how to determine whether the respondent has the possibility of continuing to endanger society must be comprehensively judged based on the respondent's past behavior and the evidence in the case. A medical institution's assessment is only an evaluation of the recovery of the patient's condition; the law does not grant medical institutions the right to assess the possibility of a patient continuing to endanger society. In this case, the respondent's illness was persecutory delusional disorder; he frequently imagined that others wanted to kill him, and when going out, he was afraid of being harmed and inevitably carried defensive tools such as knives. If left untreated and without restraint, the respondent would inevitably go out, and his behavior of carrying a knife when going out would have the possibility of endangering society. Therefore, the opinion of the agent ad litem was not adopted.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Shui Changbing, Jiang Haiyi, Dai Keguo)

Guiding Case No. 64

Liu Chaojie v. China Mobile Communications Group Jiangsu Co., Ltd., Xuzhou Branch — dispute over telecom service contract

(Discussed and approved by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, released on June 30, 2016)

Keywords: civil / telecom service contract / duty to inform / validity period / breach of contract

Ruling Gist

1. Where a business operator does not expressly specify restrictions or conditions on a certain commodity or service in a standard form contract, and fails to prove that such restrictions or conditions were clearly communicated to and accepted by the consumer at the time of contract formation, such restrictions or conditions shall have no effect on the consumer.

2. Where a telecom service enterprise fails to inform the consumer at the time of contract formation that a certain service is subject to a validity period restriction, and later restricts or discontinues the service on the ground that the validity period has expired during contract performance, such action constitutes a breach of contract and the enterprise shall bear liability for breach of contract.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 39 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

On November 24, 2009, the plaintiff Liu Chaojie applied for a "Shenzhouxing Standard Card" at the business hall of the defendant, China Mobile Communications Group Jiangsu Co., Ltd., Xuzhou Branch (hereinafter "Mobile Xuzhou Branch"), with mobile phone number 1590520xxxx, and the payment method was prepaid. The plaintiff prepaid RMB 50 in service fees on the spot and participated in a promotion by Mobile Xuzhou Branch of "recharge RMB 50 and get an additional RMB 50." In the business acceptance form attached to the "China Mobile Communications Customer Network Access Service Agreement," both parties agreed on their respective rights and obligations. Article 1 of Item 4, "Assumption of Special Circumstances," provided: "Under the following circumstances, Party B has the right to suspend or restrict Party A's mobile communication services, and Party B shall not be liable for any losses incurred by Party A as a result: (1) failure to deduct payment due to non-Party B reasons such as the sealing-up, freezing, or insufficient balance of Party A's bank account; (2) Party A's prepaid amount is used up and Party A fails to replenish funds in a timely manner (including where the prepaid account balance is insufficient to deduct the next prepaid charge)."

On July 5, 2010, the plaintiff recharged RMB 50 online via UnionPay card on China Mobile's official website business hall. On November 7, 2010, when the plaintiff used the mobile phone number, he found that the number had been suspended. The plaintiff went to the defendant's business hall to inquire and learned that the defendant had suspended mobile communication services on October 23, 2010, due to the expiration of the validity period for the service charges, at which time the account balance was RMB 11.70. The plaintiff believed that the defendant's unilateral termination of services constituted a breach of contract and therefore filed a lawsuit with the court.

Judgment

The Quanshan District People's Court of Xuzhou City rendered a civil judgment (No. 240, 2011, Quan Shang Chu Zi) on June 16, 2011: The defendant, China Mobile Communications Group Jiangsu Co., Ltd., Xuzhou Branch, shall, within ten days from the date the judgment takes effect, cancel the validity period restriction on the plaintiff Liu Chaojie's mobile phone number 1590520xxxx and restore mobile communication services for that number. After the judgment of first instance was pronounced, the defendant appealed, but during the second instance, it applied to withdraw the appeal. The judgment of first instance has become legally effective.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held: The right to know of a telecom user is a fundamental right when receiving telecom services. When a user applies for telecom services, the telecom service operator must clearly explain the content of the telecom service, including service functions, fee collection methods and payment time, and procedures for reporting faults. If the user consumes without knowing the true situation of the telecom service, it would deprive the user of the right to choose telecom services, and the user would fail to achieve the true purpose of telecom consumption.

According to Article 39 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, when entering into a contract using standard terms, the party providing the standard terms shall determine the rights and obligations between the parties in accordance with the principle of fairness, and shall draw the other party's attention in a reasonable manner to the terms that exempt or limit its liability, and shall explain such terms upon the other party's request. The telecom service operator, as the party providing the standard terms in the telecom service contract, shall determine the rights and obligations of the telecom user in accordance with the principle of fairness, and the content of the rights and obligations must comply with the legislative purpose of protecting the legitimate rights and interests of telecom users and telecom service operators and promoting the healthy development of the telecom industry, and shall effectively inform the other party of the terms that exempt or limit its liability and explain them. The business acceptance form and network access service agreement constitute the main content of the telecom service contract and define the rights and obligations of both parties. Item 4 of the network access service agreement provides for circumstances in which the service may be suspended or restricted, and Item 5 provides for circumstances in which the agreement may be terminated, the number retrieved, and service ended. Neither item provides for suspension, rescission, or termination of the contract due to expiration of the validity period. The validity period restriction on service charges directly affects the normal use of the plaintiff's mobile phone number. Once the validity period expires, it will lead to service suspension and retrieval of the number. Therefore, the defendant had a clear and truthful duty to inform the plaintiff of this restriction, and this duty should have been fulfilled before entering into the telecom service contract. If the defendant failed to inform the plaintiff before contract formation, even if it informed the plaintiff at the payment stage, the plaintiff's right to choose would still be deprived, which violates the principles of fairness and good faith. The defendant argued that "it had informed the plaintiff of the validity period through single-invoice receipts, brochures, and text messages," but failed to provide valid evidence to prove this. In summary, the defendant neither included the validity period content in the telecom service contract nor provided valid evidence to prove that it had clearly informed the plaintiff of the validity period restriction. The defendant's actions in suspending service and retrieving the number constituted a breach of contract, and it shall bear liability for breach of contract by continuing to perform. Therefore, the plaintiff's claim to "cancel the validity period restriction on the plaintiff's service charges and continue to perform the contract" was supported in accordance with law.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Wang Ping, Zhao Zengyao, Li Li)
